articles.summary: Marty Erlichman, who discovered Barbra Streisand and in over 60 years as her manager helped shape and guide her career, has died. He was 97. Erlichman first saw Streisand when he went to see an old friend, comedian Phil Leeds, perform. In 1991, he recalled that night.

articles.title: Shahrbanoo Sadat and Jelena Maksimović Hit Back at Discrimination in Film Funding at Tokyo Festival Talk
articles.summary: A lack of funding, and ignorance in the institutions that control it, keeps women at an inherent disadvantage in the film industry, Afghan director Shahrbanoo Sadat said at a Tokyo International Film Festival talk on the future of women’s cinema.
body: The talk, part of the festival’s Tokyo Talk sessions at the TIFF Lounge in Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, also featured Serbian director Jelena Maksimović, whose “Until the Day Ends” played in Venice’s Orizzonti section. Sadat, now based in Germany, saw her latest feature “No Good Men” open the 76th Berlinale before screening in Tokyo. Film scholar and presenter Takasaki Ikuko moderated.

The session followed other reflections on women’s careers in film at the festival, both in its Women’s Empowerment section and at an animation symposium held earlier the same day on the past, present and future of four women working as directors in the anime industry.

The panel set out to discuss how women and feminism are presented in Sadat’s and Maksimović’s films and beyond, but it turned mostly to the practical, financial barriers standing in the way of more films directed by women.
Both filmmakers said getting the means to make a film often requires a certain conformity.

articles.title: Dave Bautista Reveals He’s Gained 20 Pounds of Muscle Ahead of Playing Kratos in ‘God of War’ Series
articles.summary: Dave Bautista is once again showing off his muscle gains ahead of stepping into the role of Kratos for the highly anticipated “God of War” series. The “Guardians of the Galaxy” actor last gave fans a glimpse into his transformation two months ago, saying he’d begun weight training again but still…
body: In August, Bautista signed on to play Kratos, replacing Ryan Hurst, who was originally cast and suffered an on-set injury that led Prime Video to replace him. (Hurst tore his bicep on set and required surgery that would have delayed production into 2027.) Filming began in Vancouver in February, but the production will have to reshoot all scenes with Hurst using Bautista.

The series will follow the story of the two most recent “God of War” video games, which follow Kratos as he raises his ten-year-old son Atreus (Callum Vinson) while battling gods of the Norse pantheon. Per the logline, “Father and son Kratos and Atreus embark on a journey to spread the ashes of their wife and mother, Faye. Through their adventures, Kratos tries to teach his son to be a better god, while Atreus tries to teach his father how to be a better human.”
Prime Video gave “ God of War ” a two-season order, with the two seasons set to shoot back-to-back.
Bautista has starred in films including “My Spy,” “Knock at the Cabin,” “The Wrecking Crew” and more. He will next appear in “Road House 2” and the “Highlander” reboot.

articles.title: Jakarta World Cinema Plans to Revive First Feature Competition With International Jury
articles.summary: Jakarta World Cinema aims to bring back its First Feature Competition next year, open to filmmakers from around the world and judged by an international jury. This year’s edition did not accept submissions.
body: Next year, the team wants to bring in international jury members with strong filmographies, so the category can open to submissions from filmmakers worldwide.

The festival sits between October’s Jakarta Film Week and the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival at the end of November. Its lineup is made up of “80-90% award-winning films from Cannes, Berlin, Venice and Sundance,” according to Frederica, executive director of Jakarta World Cinema and director of KlikFilm, who oversees acquisitions.
“We travel to [different] film markets, Berlin, Toronto, Cannes, etc.,” says Frederica, adding that the festival aims to bring the year’s most important art films to local audiences.

This year’s edition has 102 theatrical titles, the most in the festival’s history, out of a total program of 207. Programming director Daniel Irawan says the goal for next year is to expand the lineup and keep working with its main venue, CGV Grand Indonesia, to increase audience capacity.

articles.title: Dustin Hoffman Says Filming ‘The Graduate’ Was a ‘Terrible Experience’ and Director Mike Nichols Made Katharine Ross Slap Him 27 Times for a Scene He ‘Didn’t Even Use’
articles.summary: Dustin Hoffman, who shot to fame after starring as Ben Braddock in Mike Nichols’ classic film “The Graduate,” has opened up about his experience shooting the 1967 comedy-drama in a recent essay for The New Yorker, which he described as having been a “terrible experience” despite the fact that the…
body: Hoffman writes that the film “exacerbated all my insecurities from the start.” “When my agent said that Mike was interested in me, I didn’t even want to try out for the part. I had read the Charles Webb novel that Mike was adapting, and it was obvious that I was all wrong for Benjamin. A track star and straight-A student, the head of the debate team—this was an affluent, all-American kid, whose surname was ‘Braddock.’ Why would you cast a person who looks as ethnic as I do to play the ultimate Wasp? It made absolutely no sense.” He continued, explaining that his agent convinced him to screen-test for the role, which he ultimately got.

However, beyond Hoffman’s worries about his ability to play Ben, he also writes that Nichols was “frequently sour” on set, a “shocking, destabilizing” change from his personality during rehearsals. “I often felt that I was about to be fired. When we were shooting some of the film’s most famous sequences, I remember thinking, I have no fucking idea what I’m doing,” said Hoffman.
He also notes that while the director was “irritable with everyone,” there was a “certain sadism” that “seemed to creep in” only with him.

articles.title: Director Michael Mann accidentally shoots himself in the leg at gun range
articles.summary: Mann taken to hospital with superficial injury after weapon accidentally discharged while holstered. Hollywood director Michael Mann has been taken to the hospital following an apparently accidental shooting at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the Associated Press.
body: Mann, 83, reportedly shot himself in the leg while at the The Range LA. The news was first reported on celebrity website TMZ. He sustained what his representative described as a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

The Los Angeles Police Department told the Hollywood Reporter that officers had responded to The Range LA at around 4pm. “Responding units’ investigation determined the shooting to be accidental. The subject was transported to a local hospital in stable condition,” a LAPD spokesperson said.

Mann is one of the best known long-standing directors in Hollywood, known for major works like Manhunter, The Last of the Mohicans and Heat. His most recent move was Ferrari, starring Adam Driver and Penelope Cruz, that was released in 2023. Mann also helped created the hit 1980s TV cop show Miami Vice.
TMZ reported that Mann had been trying to holster his weapon when the gun accidentally discharged. Emergency services were then called and he was taken to a hospital.
points: Mann taken to hospital with superficial injury after weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

articles.title: Tokyo: ‘Diamond Diplomacy’ Doc Tracks the History of Baseball in Japan and Its Impact on U.S. Relations
articles.summary: Film traces stories of players from both countries crossing the Pacific, racial and diplomatic tensions, wartime baseball, through to the phenomenon that is Shohei Ohtani.
body: Examining 150 years of Japan -US relations through the prism of a common passion for baseball, Diamond Diplomacy deftly interweaves the story of Japanese yakyu with issues of history, geopolitics and race.

“People from MLB told me that I had great timing and was making the film at just the right moment with Ohtani’s success,” said Romer at a screening before the film’s official Japan premiere at Tokyo International Film Festival. “But it was just coincidence. I started researching this film 12 years ago and it took me years of making money and raising money to fund it.”

Having landed a $600,000 National Endowment for the Humanities grant, more than half of the funding was cancelled in April 2025 as swingeing DOGE cuts suddenly took effect. Former American diplomat Glen S. Fukushima stepped in with $300,000 that allowed the film to be finished.
Author Robert Whiting, whose books helped introduce the peculiarities of baseball in Japan to the wider world, is one of the documentary’s talking heads.
points: Film traces stories of players from both countries crossing the Pacific, racial and diplomatic tensions, wartime baseball, through to the phenomenon that is Shohei Ohtani.

articles.title: Book to Scream: How Universal Orlando’s Halloween Event Embraced Horror’s Literary Roots for 35 Years
articles.summary: Members of the Halloween Horror Nights' creative team go inside this year's 'Hellraiser' maze and menu, detail over three decades of literary-inspired houses and scare zones, and examine how one of their original shows is growing the event's audience with readers.
body: Inside Universal Studios Orlando Resort’s Hellraiser house, past the shirtless mannequin of a kneeling Frank Cotton and the narrow hallway where blue light seeps through crumbling clapboard, is a sight to show you: Halloween Horror Nights 35’s towering recreation of the Lament Configuration. Along with it, five to seven minutes of legendary suffering only possible in the world of Clive Barker’s cinematic and literary nightmare.

Outside, art director Cam Carbia’s design sees the cursed, mechanical plot device flayed open, its “doorway” to hell speckled with embedded programmable LED lights, restrained by chains and ripped flesh. Inside, scenic designer Dylan Kollath constructed a disorienting labyrinth of pleasure and pain out of a big-screen world based on Barker’s novella The Hellbound Heart. “When we pitched to Clive, he was very adamant that this haunted house would feature both,” says Lora Sauls, Assistant Director, Entertainment, UOR. “He made sure that our teams didn’t take out the sexual layer of those films.”

articles.title: Clayface Concept Art Shows Disturbing Alternate Designs For DC Universe Villain
articles.summary: Clayface's transformation is relatively gradual in his solo movie, but early concept designs put a more unnerving spin on the DC Universe villain.
body: The DC Universe has delivered its first properly scary film. Though a bit shapeless, "Clayface" is an effective and very gory body horror movie. Drawing from a script by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini (and borrowing a whole lot from Sam Raimi's "Darkman" along the way), director James Watkins re-imagines the titular Batman villain as a tragic but still very horrific movie monster here.

Indeed, Tom Rhys Harries's Matt Hagen goes through quite a transformation in the film, and it's heavily reliant on implication ( much like the special effects in James Cameron's "The Terminator" ). A creepy eye here, a spiky hand there — it's really comic book-y until the final act finally reveals the mud-like Clayface fans know from DC's comics. Now, concept artist Carlos Huante has now taken to Instagram to share some of his early design work on "Clayface" before the film was properly greenlit by Warner Bros. Pictures.
points: Clayface's transformation is relatively gradual in his solo movie, but early concept designs put a more unnerving spin on the DC Universe villain.

articles.title: Legendary Sci-Fi Writer Harlan Ellison Wrote An Underrated Daredevil Story For Marvel
articles.summary: Harlan Ellison wrote a compelling (if lesser-known) Daredevil story for Marvel Comics, with the sci-fi legend crafting a tale of robots, deathtraps, and more.
body: Harlan Ellison is one of the defining science fiction writers of the 20th Century, and one of the lights on the fuse of his imagination was the comic books he read as a child. He never outgrew them, either, maintaining a huge archive of his comic collection well into adulthood that he called the "living beating heart of [his] house." He praised Jack Kirby, co-creator of the Fantastic Four, the X-Men, and the Avengers, as a "master of the form" for his series, "The Forever People," at DC.

Ellison's bibliography is scattered with comic book credits, including and beyond Marvel and DC superheroes. Alongside artist Bernie Wrightson, he devised the story for 1971's "Batman" #237, a Halloween issue titled "Night of the Reaper." He also helped author the 1985 Marvel one-shot "Heroes for Hope," an "exquisite corpse" issue featuring the X-Men with contributed pages from many other writers, including Stephen King and George R.R. Martin, along with Alan Moore ( who wrote a chilling three pages X-Men story about Magneto ).
points: Harlan Ellison wrote a compelling (if lesser-known) Daredevil story for Marvel Comics, with the sci-fi legend crafting a tale of robots, deathtraps, and more.

articles.summary: In the since-deleted photo, the lifestyle guru appears to be wearing ripped clothing and holding a clipboard with the message, "I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!"
body: Martha Stewart is addressing the backlash over a since-deleted photo of her Halloween costume, where she appears to be depicting a homeless person.

In the photo posted on Instagram before being quickly deleted, TMZ reported that the lifestyle guru and media mogul was seen in ripped clothing with dirt on her face. She was also holding a clipboard with a message that read “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!”
The Hollywood Reporter has also reached out to Stewart’s rep for comment.
TMZ reported that the photo was included in an Instagram carousel promoting candles she sells on QVC. “My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!!!” the post’s caption read.

articles.title: Josh Hartnett's Twisty Neo-Noir Thriller With Bruce Willis Is Streaming For Free
articles.summary: Josh Hartnett has said he had a great time working opposite stars like Bruce Willis on this wild neo-noir thriller, which is currently streaming for free.
body: Josh Hartnett once starred in a darkly comedic neo-noir thriller, and you can stream it for free at this very moment. Co-starring the action legend Bruce Willis as part of an impressive ensemble, "Lucky Number Slevin" didn't get its flowers back in 2006, but it's since garnered a loyal following. /Film editor Ben Pearson even counts it among his favorite movies of all time.

Streaming now on Tubi and Pluto TV, "Lucky Number Slevin" was directed by Paul McGuigan, whom Hartnett had previously worked with on 2004's "Wicker Park." The movie focuses on a case of mistaken identity, which puts a man named Slevin (Hartnett) in the middle of a war between two rival New York crime lords. Under the watchful eyes of Detective Brikowski (Stanley Tucci) and an assassin named Goodkat (Willis), Slevin must devise a plan to save his skin as these forces converge around him.
